Stage 2 Frontend Summary

Interactive Dashboard & Data Visualization

Author: Ethan Bayarsaikhan (Person 2) · Stage 2  |  Verified: 2026-11-06
This page summarises the Stage 2 dashboard and its evidence. Person numbering follows the team’s division of work.

01 / Delivery at a Glance

4visualizations
11browser screenshots
3API action buttons
0build steps (Chart.js via CDN)

Stage 2 builds the whole dashboard on top of Stage 1’s merged main: a static site in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Chart.js from a CDN, so there is no build step and the folder deploys to an Azure Static Web App as-is. A single fetch helper with one API_BASE_URL reads the four endpoints and fills four charts, a searchable recipe table and the status badges.

Status: Stage 2 is complete and evidenced against the local Function host at http://localhost:7071. All four visualizations, the search box, the diet filter, the three action buttons and Previous/Next pagination work; the execution-time badge shows each call’s server time and browser round trip, and a red error banner appears when the API is unreachable. Eleven browser screenshots are archived in stage2/screenshots/. Moving to Azure is Stage 3 — only the one line in config.js changes.

03 / Structure and Files

Page open→apiGet() fetch helper→/insights · /recipes · /clusters→Charts, table, badges
FilePurpose
index.htmlPage layout, following the course UI skeleton: status bar, four chart cards, controls and the recipe table
styles.cssAll styling; colours and sizes match the skeleton
config.jsAPI_BASE_URL — the only line that changes between local and Azure
api.jsapiGet() fetch helper: error handling, the red error banner and the execution-time badge
charts.jsBar, pie and scatter charts with Chart.js; the heatmap is an HTML/CSS grid
recipes.jsRecipe table, search, diet filter and Previous/Next pagination
app.jsLoads everything on page open and wires up the buttons

config.js sets API_BASE_URL to http://localhost:7071/api for local runs; for the live site Stage 3 changes it to the Azure Function URL ending in /api with no trailing slash. All API text is inserted with textContent, never innerHTML, so dataset values can never run as HTML.

05 / Charts and Controls

Four visualizations

  • Bar average macronutrients per diet type, from /insights.
  • Pie recipe count per diet type, from summary.diet_counts.
  • Heatmap nutrient correlations as a CSS grid (Chart.js has no heatmap type); opacity is correlation strength, blue positive and red negative, with protein and fat the most related (0.48).
  • Scatter protein vs carbs coloured by k-means cluster from /clusters?k=3, centres marked ×.

Controls

  • Search box and a diet dropdown (All, Dash, Keto, Mediterranean, Paleo, Vegan).
  • Get Nutritional Insights / Get Recipes / Get Clusters buttons; each shows “Loading…” and is disabled while its request runs.
  • Recipe table with Previous / Next pagination, 20 rows per page.
  • Execution-time badge showing the Function’s own time and the browser round trip, labelled by endpoint.
  • A red error banner when the API cannot be reached; it hides again after the next success.

Design choices. The scatter plot draws every 4th of the 7,806 points (about 1,950) so it stays readable, while the legend still shows each cluster’s full count; its axes are fixed at 0–600 g protein and 0–1,000 g carbs, which keeps 99.2% of recipes on scale instead of squashing them into one corner.

06 / Running Locally

# 1) start the backend (Git Bash)
cd stage1
source .venv311/Scripts/activate
func start --port 7071

# 2) serve the dashboard in a second terminal
cd stage2
py -3.11 -m http.server 5500

# 3) open the dashboard
http://localhost:5500

Port 5500 matters: the backend’s local CORS setting only allows http://localhost:5500 and http://127.0.0.1:5500. Opening index.html straight from the file system will not work. Handing off to Stage 3 is a one-line change: point API_BASE_URL at the live Function App and add the Static Web App’s origin to the Function App’s CORS list.
